title: Skilled Builders and a Day of Rest
overview: God names the craftsmen who will build the tent of worship, reminds Israel that the weekly day of rest still stands, and gives Moses the stone tablets.

parts.label: Bezalel chosen (vv. 1-5)
parts.note: God picks Bezalel, from the tribe of Judah, to lead the building work, and says his skill in metal, stone and wood comes from being filled with God's Spirit. His grandfather Hur may be the Hur who helped lead Israel earlier in the book, though that is not certain.

parts.label: Oholiab and the team (v. 6)
parts.note: A partner from the tribe of Dan is added, along with every skilled worker God has given ability to. Some interpreters see meaning in pairing a leader from prominent Judah with one from a less prominent tribe, though the text does not explain the choice.

parts.label: What they will make (vv. 7-11)
parts.note: This list recaps everything described in the previous chapters: the portable worship tent, the sacred chest and its lid, the furniture, the priests' clothing, and the special oil and incense. The builders must follow the instructions exactly, though there was still room for real artistry in how the work was done.

parts.label: The Sabbath as a sign (vv. 12-17)
parts.note: The weekly day of rest is called a lasting sign between God and Israel, echoing God resting after making the world, and many interpreters think it appears here so no one would work on it even for this holy project. The penalty is stated bluntly as death, and scholars are unsure whether being "cut off from their people" meant exile, execution, or death left in God's hands.

parts.label: The stone tablets (v. 18)
parts.note: As the long meeting on Mount Sinai ends, God gives Moses two stone tablets, understood to hold the Ten Commandments. Saying they were written by "the finger of God" stresses that these words come directly from God.

think: Is there anything you would refuse to let work take over, even when the work feels urgent or important?
